title: CORS is a browser rule

blocks.md:
## Not Node, not this sandbox

The **browser** asks: may this page’s origin read that response? CORS is an HTTP header conversation the *browser* enforces. A server can send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. The browser decides whether page JS may read the body.

Node `fetch` and this lesson stub do **not** simulate CORS. `capabilities.network: false` also does not claim to be an OS firewall. The idea still matters when you later ship a page. The fox’s board in a browser is not the same as a Node script on the desk.

blocks.promptMd: Who decides whether page code may read another origin’s body?

choices.md: The browser, for that page’s origin

blocks.explainMd: CORS is a browser rule for front-end origins. Node and this stub do not simulate it.
A server can send Access-Control-Allow-Origin. The browser decides whether page JS may read the body.
